title: Getting Away With It
paragraphs: I found a completely new type of milestone post. User Turbulent-Top-3892, reached their milestone, but in a very unexpected plot twist, they did not reveal the amount of bitcoin stacked (see screenshot)!!! Clearly, Turbulent-Top-3892 is no passing tourist in this bitcoin sphere, and is well aware of the first rule, and probably most often repeated rule for bitcoin holders: Never reveal your bitcoin holdings! Turbulent-Top-3892 was willing to put their ego aside, for the sake of their safety & security.

The irony is that by choosing to protect themselves, Turbulent-Top-3892 has inadvertently created a new kind of milestone post — one where the celebration exists but the evidence does not. When safety and security are potentially at risk, it is a bold if not risky move to post your bitcoin holdings on the internet, making yourself a potential target. Turbulent-Top-3892, avoids making themselves an immediate target, but not completely. Potential scammers would still be aware that they hold bitcoin, only the amount of bitcoin is in question. That said, due to the deflationary nature of bitcoin, given enough time, even what is considered small amounts of bitcoin today, can be a small fortune in the future. So Turbulent-Top-3892, has only reduced their potential risks, but has not completely eliminated it.

I cannot deny it, even though I understand and respect Turbulent-Top-3892's decision not to reveal their holdings, I can't help but wonder, what is their milestone? 0.5 BTC, 1 BTC, 3 BTC or 15 BTC? Looking at the comments, I was not the only person either. User Hedgehog0206, couldn't help but ask, "Just out of curiosity how much do you have now? I only have like 500 dollars worth of BC rn haha", and was promptly downvoted for trying to get OP to break the most important rule of bitcoin, LOL.

So yes, I do not have a new data point to track with Turbulent-Top-3892's post. But the milestone has still been tracked, if not numerically. Which leaves me wondering, will this type of post become the new norm as bitcoin continues to increase in value? If so, the life of this hyperbitcoinization tracker may be shorter lived than I would have even anticipated. It would still be interesting to see if this type of post becomes more frequent. Time will tell.

Today's musing aims to capture a moment in time within this data set, in two meaningful ways. Currently, looking at the milestone clustering chart, see the screenshot below, there is a numerically significant, yet outdated (will explain in a bit) milestone reached. The table shows that there are currently 21 milestone posts, from users that have reached the significant milestone of attaining 1 bitcoin.

This is a significant feat due to the fact that as the price of bitcoin continues to increase, it will inevitably become even more rare for individuals to achieve. I imagine such posts will become rarer with time. Then of course there is the numerology of it. 21 is a special milestone in the bitcoin world, for the simple fact that the maximum amount of bitcoin that will ever exist, is 21 million. So, these posts, taken at face value, represent 21 individuals that have reached the incredibly rare milestone of acquiring 1 whole bitcoin.
Alas, this table is now outdated, as I believe I have at least two more posts of users claiming this rare feat. But I wanted to acknowledge this moment, before I updated the data.

While on the topic of this chart, I also wanted to point out that the next most frequent milestone posting is for the achievement of acquiring 0.1 BTC, which at the time of writing this (Sunday April 19, 2026) costs $7,447, is no small feat. The total number of posts celebrating this milestone, currently stands at 17. I am calling it now. I fully expect the number of milestone posts celebrating 0.1 BTC, to pass the total amount of posts celebrating the 1 BTC milestone, by the end of this year. When exactly will this happen? I am not sure, I just have a gut feeling that it will happen this year. Whenever it does happen, it will be a very strong indicator for the hyperbitcoinization thesis. Stay tuned!

title: 1009 Days
preview: 1000 days. 1009 to be exact. Where did the time fly? To be honest I only vaguely remember when I got the idea for this project. Like many people in the Bitcoin space, my initial serious entry started in 2017...
paragraphs: 1000 days. 1009 to be exact. Where did the time fly? To be honest I only vaguely remember when I got the idea for this project. Like many people in the Bitcoin space, my initial serious entry into Bitcoin started in 2017 (had exposure to Bitcoin in 2009….yes really, and 2013, but both times I dismissed it). 2017 I had just gotten a warehouse job after being unemployed for 6 months, and I wanted to start investing, and figured I would purchase small amounts of Bitcoin when able. During that time I remember scrolling r/Bitcoin and seeing all the milestone posts of people reaching multiple Bitcoins owned, and their future plans to stack more. I thought their posts were interesting, but I had not learned about hyperbitcoinization as yet, so that was that.

By 2023, as you can see by the early screenshots that I have collected, I was fully onboard with the concept of hyperbitcoinization, and figured these posts would be an excellent way to document this in real time. I figured no point in going back looking for older posts, I'm documenting my experience.

Fast forward to late last year. And I said to myself, "you have hundreds (lol, will get back to this) of these screenshots, time to start posting about this project and show the world that hyperbitcoinization is indeed happening, as shown through this very unique lens!" So I started building this site.

So you're probably wondering, 1000 days, 3 years, and all you have to show for it is just over 135 posts!?!? I assure you when I completed my first count (106 posts at the time, I believe) of all the posts I had collected over the years, I too was absolutely surprised. I said there is no way these are all the posts I have collected, I should have at least 300 by now. But I checked and rechecked. The count was accurate. So what happened?

First my method of finding posts was not intentional, in the sense that I never went looking for these posts, I simply captured them as they popped up in my feed. I'm a chronic daily Reddit user (judge if you must, I have no shame about this!). This was/is a side project for me, I didn't want it to take up a considerable amount of time. Does this approach to collecting/finding milestone posts potentially limit the amount of posts I would find? Absolutely and I am sure I have missed more than a few posts over these past three years.

Second, however, whatever amount of posts I did miss, I have a very strong hunch it is not a significant amount to affect the data meaningfully. Why do I believe this? For the simple fact that a very common piece of advice in r/Bitcoin and the Bitcoin community at large, is to never reveal your holdings. Many times in the comment section of these milestone posts, other redditors will reprimand posters for breaking this very rule.

So I speculate that the ones that choose to post in spite of the rule, are a minority of a minority. There are more than likely far more people who reach their milestones, and choose either not to post — or not to post on Reddit (where I get the majority of my posts). If I am right about this, this can explain, at least in some part, why the amount of posts I have collected over the years has been so sparse.
So here we are now, excited for a hyperbitcoinized world!

title: The First Post-Launch Entry
preview: It's the first of the month, Sunday March 1st, 2026, and with that first comes another very special first. I have just uploaded the very first new post since this site went live, and the special honor goes to u/Fall-For-October...
paragraphs: It's the first of the month, Sunday March 1st, 2026, and with that first comes another very special first. I have just uploaded the very first new post since this site went live, and the special honor goes to u/Fall-For-October who just reached a milestone of 0.7 BTC — or 70 million satoshis. Whether this post exists because of this site or in spite of it, I may never know — but I'm glad it's here. Who knows if you will ever see this, but here's to hoping you do ultimately reach that goal of 1 full Bitcoin. Godspeed. And to the other posts coming here after, I can't wait to see you reach your own personal milestones!

title: Launch Day
preview: Today, after nearly three years of quietly collecting data, GoalPost BTC goes live. No fanfare, no announcement — just a site that exists now, doing the thing I built it to do.
paragraphs: Today, Saturday February 28, 2026, is a special day for me because I finally launched this site — goalpostbtc.com — a site that was three years in the making. But the culmination of years of work to the realization of a goal is not the only reason today is special for the launch of this site. It's also special because today marks the point at which the data collected for this site will not entirely be of the same type as data collected after today.

Cause and effect is at play here, as it is in all things. It only takes one pair of eyes to change the scope of the data collected forever. Will people who become aware of the site be motivated to post their milestones in hopes that I'll see it and their milestone will be forever immortalized on this site? Or will the pendulum swing in the opposite direction? Will people be less motivated to post their milestone achievements, knowing that their posts may be captured forever, even if they delete their post or comment.

As with many things in life, the truth more than likely lands somewhere between the two extremes. In any case, for everyone who finds their way here, I hope you find my little effort to document the hyperbitcoinization of the world as interesting as I do!
